key_insight: Combining spatial and temporal information improves micro-CT segmentation, helping distinguish real pore-space and fluid changes from segmentation errors.
engineering_relevance: More reliable pore-volume and permeability estimates support analysis of geological carbon storage, underground hydrogen storage and groundwater contaminant transport.
method: Use a transformer-based 4D framework to segment sequential 3D micro-CT images.
Resolve ambiguous phase assignments using spatial and temporal context.
Quantify pore evolution and fluid displacement without per-image parameter adjustment.
evidence_signal: Tests on mineral dissolution showed improvements over an equivalent 3D model, with permeability trends verified using reference segmentations and flow simulations; benefits transferred to another dissolution sample without retraining and extended to two fluid-displacement datasets.
watch_item: Transfer beyond the tested datasets and computational requirements for long 3D image sequences remain to be established.
paper_title: Spatiotemporal learning improves quantification of pore-space evolution and fluid displacement
